Key observations from the test image:
- Lower stem/root area near soil line
- **Distinctive blue/teal fungal growth** on the stem surface
- Brown/rotted tissue
- Root decay visible

The blue fungal growth on roots/lower stem is a hallmark of **Sudden Death Syndrome** (SDS description: "Roots may show surface blue fungal growth in moist conditions"). Let me confirm with reference images.

The SDS reference image is a near-perfect match — same blue/teal fungal growth on the lower stem/root tissue, same brown decayed stem structure. This is the diagnostic "blue fungal growth on roots in moist conditions" described for Sudden Death Syndrome.

Fusarium shows internal vascular discoloration (cut stem view), and Phytophthora shows whole-plant wilting — neither matches the blue surface fungal growth in the test image.
